To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found that the MBL1 gene can underlie the QTL for immunoglobin A levels on Oar22 and that the ADAMTS gene on Oar18 can be important for GIN resistance.

22 SNPs were identified as being associated with PCV (six SNPs), ln FEC (seven), and FAMCHA scores (nine) in Djallonké lambed from Burkina Fasa and that the SNPs accounted for a total of 18.76%, 21.24%, and 34.36% of the phenotypical variance for PCV (six), ln FEC (7), and FA MACHA scores (nine), respectively.
we identified a total of seven QTLs and 34 potential candidate-gene regions that may be involved in PCV, lnFEC, or FAMACHA eye scores in Djallonké lambeds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel candidate genes that may contribute to the genetic improvement of GIN resistance traits in local sheep populations.
the identification of genomic regions and potential candidate genes for GIN parasite resistance traits in local sheep populations managed under harsh environments.
the identification of genomic regions and potential candidate genes of functional relevance for the studied traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the identified genomic regions and candidate gene for GIN resistance in Djallonké can contribute to the development of a genomic selection strategy for the improvement of GIN resistance in small ruminants.
the identified genomic regions are of functional importance for the traits analyzed, but more research is needed to elucidate their role in GIN resistance.
this research contributes to the identification and validation of novel genomic regions and candidate functional genes for GIN resistance in Djallonké ewes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OAR2 region is the most important for GIN resistance in Djallonké lambed in Burkina Faso, and the TRIB3 gene can be a good candidate for the trait.

the OAR2, OAR3, and OAR18 chromosomes harbor genomic areas of importance for PCV, lnFEC, FAMACHA, and other related traits, and the genes ADAMTS17, MBL2, CSNK2α1, MARK1 and TRIB3 are good candidate genes for GIN resistance.
a total of 14 OAR chromosomes and 34 candidate genes are potentially involved in the regulation of PCV, lnFEC, or FAMACHA eye scores in Djallonké lambed in Burkina Faso.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genomic areas on OAR6 and OAR3 can play an important role for GIN resistance in Djallonké.

genomic regions and genes involved in GIN resistance traits in Djallonne sheep are not exclusive of specific breeds, but they are common in sheep breeds from different environments and with different levels of GIN resistance.
the identification of genomic regions and potential candidate genes related with GIN resistance traits in Djallonne sheep of Burkina-Faso is a step forward for the improvement of this trait in sheep.
